claims.text: The vidsmith tool converts markdown scripts into narrated videos with synchronized captions and visuals.
Captions and visuals in vidsmith are timed using data directly from the speech engine's word-boundary reporting.
A demonstration build of a video takes approximately sixty-two seconds to produce a thirty-two point seven second file.
The software does not require API keys or user accounts for basic operation.
FFmpeg is the only non-Python software dependency required to run the tool.
Punctuation marks are re-inserted into the caption stream from the original script because the speech engine omits them.
Users can optionally use Amazon Polly for narration by providing AWS credentials, primarily for licensing considerations.
The Polly service provides word-level timing data, allowing cuts to align precisely with spoken sentence boundaries.
Polly bills for audio and speech marks as two separate requests, effectively doubling the cost per script.
The generative engine from Polly does not support speech marks, making it unsuitable for timing captions or cuts.
Scenes are divided into shots at sentence boundaries to avoid the unnatural look of long, unbroken takes.
If a sentence exceeds the maximum shot duration, it is split at the final comma, or the plan reverts to fewer, longer shots if insufficient clips are available.
Gemini can be used to rerank stock footage candidates based on their visual content rather than just popularity.
The system rejects footage candidates that do not match the subject matter, ensuring only relevant clips are used.
Reranking costs one API call per scene because the model evaluates static preview stills rather than video files.
Background music is synthesized using detuned sine waves to create an atmospheric chord pad rather than distinct notes.
The generated music bed is automatically ducked by 8 dB when narration is present.
When footage is unavailable for a concept, the system generates a JSON specification for a diagram to be drawn in the project's theme.
Diagrams are designed to be static and never use Ken Burns effects to prevent motion distraction while viewers are reading.
The decision on which scenes to illustrate is made once to ensure consistency across different aspect ratios.
The system prefers using stock photography for thumbnails because these images are specifically composed for standalone viewing, unlike video frames or diagrams.
Thumbnail candidates are sampled from the picture track rather than the final delivery file to avoid including unwanted elements like captions or watermarks.
Thumbnail candidates must be spaced at least 2.5 seconds apart to ensure variety in the selected frames.
The check utility verifies that delivered files are consistent with each other and will exit with a non-zero status if discrepancies are found.
YouTube will reject an entire chapter list if any chapter does not begin at the 0:00 timestamp.
The system uses a unified theme configuration to ensure that all on-screen elements maintain a consistent design aesthetic.
AI image generation is intentionally excluded because free-tier image models typically exhaust their quotas immediately.
Configuration keys can be loaded from the environment or from .env files located in the project directory, its parent, or the repository root.
The pipeline skips processing stages that have already been completed on disk to save time.
The system runs 200 fast tests in a matter of seconds.
The suite includes 12 tests marked as slow that perform actual video encoding using ffmpeg.
The testing suite prevents common bugs by verifying that shot plans align with narration slots and that caption lines do not overlap.
The web service limits the render queue to three concurrent submissions to avoid system saturation.
The system returns a 429 status code when the queue is full to provide a clear explanation to the user.
Users can expose their local server to the internet using a Cloudflare quick tunnel without needing an account or a domain.
Using the -NoToken flag allows the tunnel to function without a gate, which is intended for temporary demonstrations rather than permanent setups.
The script automatically comments out existing tokens in the .env file when the -NoToken flag is active.
Exposed instances consume Pexels and Gemini quotas if they are not protected by a VIDSMITH_TOKEN.
The /healthz endpoint remains accessible without a token to facilitate uptime monitoring.
The keys field in the health check response is only provided to callers who supply a valid token.
Hugging Face Spaces provides 2 vCPU and 16 GB of memory, which is sufficient for 1080p video encoding.
Free Render instances are limited to 0.1 vCPU and 512 MB of memory.
Since August 25, 2026, Docker-based Spaces on the free cpu-basic tier are no longer supported and require a PRO subscription.
A 2 vCPU instance typically encodes video at approximately 2.2 times the speed of real-time playback.
AWS instances require at least 2 vCPUs and 2 GB of memory to successfully encode 1080p video.
Passing the VIDSMITH_TOKEN as a query parameter over plain HTTP is insecure, making the use of certificates via services like DuckDNS important.
Render deployments use a native Python runtime and fetch ffmpeg and DejaVu fonts during the build process.
The software is available under the PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 license, which permits personal, hobby, and non-profit use.
Commercial licenses are available for $49 for individuals and $299 for companies.
The edge-tts narration path is not cleared for commercial use, and users should utilize Amazon Polly for commercial projects.
Polly maintains the original caption and cut timing because it provides word-level timing information.
Polly charges for both audio and speech marks as separate requests, effectively doubling the cost based on script length.
The generative engine in Polly does not provide speech marks, which is why that option cannot be selected.
The vidsmith doctor tool identifies which keys are valid for use.
